subject: physics

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2020 (Q7) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from that paper. Physics hand-checked: λₘ ∝ 1/T, that is λₘT = b with Wien’s constant b = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K, so a hotter black body has its intensity maximum at a shorter wavelength.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The statement
lines: The wavelength at which a black body emits
the greatest amount of energy is inversely
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words inversely proportional carry it.
steps.why: The peak of the black body curve is displaced towards shorter wavelengths as the temperature rises, and that displacement is what gives the law its name.
common_mistakes: Writing λₘ ∝ T. The relation is inverse: λₘ ∝ 1/T.

recall.must_convey: That the wavelength of maximum emission is inversely proportional to the absolute temperature.
accept: lambda m is one by T
peak wavelength falls as T rises
reject: b is two point nine into ten to the minus three

steps.memory_tip: Hotter body, shorter wavelength. Heated iron turns from red to white as T rises.

steps.label: The relation and the constant

lines.text: λₘ T = b, b = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write λₘT = b together with the value of b.
steps.why: The constant fixes the product λₘT for every black body, so a single measurement of the peak wavelength gives the temperature of a distant source such as a star.
common_mistakes: Giving b without its unit. Wien’s constant is 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K.

recall.must_convey: That λₘT = b with b = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K.
accept: lambda m into T equals b
two point nine into ten to the minus three

steps.memory_tip: λₘT = b. The product is fixed, so one rises exactly as the other falls.

insider_note: Two marks — the statement in words and the relation λₘT = b. Stating it only in words leaves the second mark unearned.
